`espalier` turns a tree of rule modules into per-directory documentation agents
read, and into a linter that enforces the same rules deterministically.

The documents under `docs/` are the specification. Where the code and a
document disagree, the document is right — so most of the rules here check that
the two still point at each other, rather than checking style.

## Structure

    docs/                   the specification
      cli/                  one page per command
        [command]/
          README.MD         the page for one command
      [doc].MD              a specification document
    ignores/                the ignore lists espalier ships
      [language].gitignore  a shipped ignore list
    src/                    the implementation
      [name].ts             an implementation module
    test/                   the argument that the tool works
      [name].test.ts        a test module
    HANDOFF.MD              the record of what was decided and why
    README.MD               the front page

HANDOFF.MD and README.MD are required. Zero or more `docs/cli/[command]/`
directories may exist. For each one that does, README.MD is required. Zero or
more files matching `docs/[doc].MD` may exist. Zero or more files matching
`ignores/[language].gitignore` may exist. Zero or more files matching
`src/[name].ts` may exist. Zero or more files matching `test/[name].test.ts` may
exist. Nothing else may exist under this directory.

## Not described here

    .espalierignore       Configuration. Read by `espalier`, not by this
                          project.
    espalier.config.yaml
    espalier/
    .claude/              Editor and operating system droppings.
    .cursor/
    LICENSE               Licence and legal.
    package-lock.json     Manifests and lockfiles.
    package.json
    .gitignore            Repository metadata. Tracked on purpose, and dictated
                          by the tool that reads them rather than by this
                          project's architecture.
    tsconfig.json         Tool configuration. The tool decides the filename; the
                          project only decides the contents.
    .git/                 Version control metadata. `.gitignore` never lists
                          `.git/` — git has no need to ignore itself — so this
                          is the one exclusion no other file supplies.
    AGENTS.MD             Written by `espalier build` from the rules above.
    fixtures/             espalier's own fixtures are data: sixty configs,
                          several deliberately invalid, and a root run executing
                          all sixty is not what anyone means by it.
    dist/
    node_modules/

Nothing above describes these, so nothing here tells you how to write them. That makes them a poor place to put work that belongs in the list above: a file with nowhere legal to go is a gap to report, not one to route around.

## HANDOFF.MD — the record of what was decided and why

Every decision that cost an argument is written down here,
struck through rather than deleted when it is superseded. A reversal that
leaves no trace is a decision that will be made again.

## README.MD — the front page

Opens with a level-one heading, and links into `docs/` for
anything it only summarizes. The front page is allowed to be shorter than the
specification; it is not allowed to be a second, drifting copy of it.

## Checking your work

Run `espalier lint` before you finish. Every violation it reports arrives with
the rule text attached, so a failure tells you what to do and not only what is
wrong.

## Amending this structure

This file is generated from `espalier/`, and the structure it describes is not
yours to change. If the work does not fit — a file has nowhere legal to go, or a
rule is wrong for the task — YOU MUST stop and report the gap. YOU MUST NOT
widen a pattern, add a rule, or edit `espalier/` to make an error go away.
Deciding the shape of this project is the architect's job, and a task that
appears to require changing that shape is a task to hand back, not to unblock.
